recipes.title: Lorighittas al Sugo
recipes.description: Lorighittas al Sugo from Sardinia. A braised meat ragù preparation built on hen or chicken, onion, garlic cloves, carrot, red wine, crushed tomatoes, saffron and bay.

steps.text: Brown the hen or chicken in the oil in batches until well coloured; set aside.
Soften the onion, garlic and carrot in the same pot for 8 minutes.
Return the meat, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes and saffron and bay, season, and braise on low heat 1.5–2 hours until the meat is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the gnocchetti sardi in well-salted water; reserve a mugful of water.
Toss the pasta through the ragù with a little pasta water. Serve with grated Pecorino.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Filindeu in Brodo
recipes.description: Filindeu in Brodo from Sardinia. A filled pasta in clear broth preparation built on fresh filindeu ('threads of god' — hand-pulled semolina lace), clear capon or chicken broth.

items.name: fresh filindeu ('threads of God' — hand-pulled semolina lace)

steps.text: Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and check the seasoning.
Slip in the filindeu ('threads of God' — hand-pulled semolina lace) and cook until they float and the pasta is tender, about 3–4 minutes for fresh.
Ladle into warm bowls with plenty of broth.
Serve with grated Parmigiano at the table.

recipes.storage: Keep pasta and broth separate; combine when serving. 2 days refrigerated.
recipes.freezing: Freeze broth and uncooked pasta separately up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat the broth, then cook the pasta in it fresh.
chefTips: The broth must be genuinely good and clear — it is half the dish.
Cook the pasta right in the broth so it seasons the bowl.
variations: 'In brodo' for feast days; the same pasta is served 'asciutti' with butter on other days.
Passatelli (a Parmesan-and-crumb dough pressed through a ricer) is made the same way.
commonMistakes: Boiling the broth hard and clouding it.
Over-filling the bowl with pasta and skimping on broth.

recipes.title: Spaghetti alla Bottarga
recipes.description: Spaghetti alla Bottarga from Sardinia. A raw bottarga finish preparation built on spaghetti, bottarga di muggine (grey mullet roe), garlic cloves, extra-virgin olive oil, chilli flakes.

steps.text: Warm the oil gently with the garlic and chilli; discard the garlic.
Stir most of the grated bottarga into the warm (not hot) oil to loosen it into a paste.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the spaghetti. Cook until al dente, about 1 minute less than the packet. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta in the bottarga oil with a good splash of pasta water to emulsify.
Finish with parsley and shavings of bottarga over the top. No cheese.

recipes.freezing: Not suitable.
recipes.reheating: Not recommended.
chefTips: Bottarga is salty and best kept mostly raw — heat makes it bitter and grainy.
Emulsify well with pasta water so it coats rather than sits in a puddle of oil.
variations: A little lemon zest lifts it.
Sardinia serves it on spaghetti or spaghettoni.
commonMistakes: Cooking the bottarga hard.
Over-salting the pasta water — the roe is very salty.

recipes.title: Zuppa Gallurese
recipes.description: Zuppa Gallurese from Sardinia. A bread & cheese bake preparation built on stale country bread or carasau, fresh pecorino or caciotta, aged pecorino, rich lamb or beef broth, saffron.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Layer the bread and sliced cheese in a deep dish, finishing with grated pecorino.
Ladle the hot broth (with saffron if using) evenly over until the bread is soaked but not swimming.
Bake 35–40 minutes until set, golden and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes; serve in wedges.

recipes.freezing: Freeze cooked portions up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered at 170°C / 340°F for 20 minutes.
chefTips: Zuppa gallurese is 'zuppa' in the old sense — soaked bread, not a liquid soup.
The broth must be well-flavoured; it is doing most of the seasoning.
variations: Add chopped parsley and mint between the layers.
Sardinian carasau bread gives a lighter, crisper result.
commonMistakes: Too much broth, turning it to mush.
Weak broth, leaving it bland.

recipes.description: Chitarra con Pallottine from Abruzzo. A meatballs in tomato sauce preparation built on minced beef, minced pork, fresh breadcrumbs, egg, pecorino romano, garlic cloves, parsley.

steps.text: Mix the meatball ingredients gently — don't compact them — and roll into balls a little smaller than a golf ball.
Brown them in the oil in batches; set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add the tomatoes and basil and bring to a simmer.
Return the meatballs and simmer gently 40 minutes, turning once, until tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the pasta and toss with some of the sauce and a little pasta water.
Serve the pasta topped with meatballs and sauce and plenty of Pecorino.

recipes.freezing: Freeze meatballs in sauce up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently in the sauce with a splash of water.

variations: All-beef for a leaner ball; add veal for the classic three-meat mix.
Bake the browned meatballs instead of frying.
commonMistakes: Over-mixing and over-rolling, making them dense.

recipes.title: Scrippelle 'mbusse
recipes.description: Scrippelle 'mbusse from Abruzzo. A crêpes in broth preparation built on plain flour, eggs, milk, parsley.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and parsley to a thin batter; rest 20 minutes.
Cook thin crêpes in a buttered pan.
Sprinkle each crêpe with grated pecorino and a little nutmeg and roll up tightly.
Cut the rolls in half or leave whole; sit 2–3 per person in warm soup bowls.
Ladle the very hot broth over and serve at once, with more pecorino.

recipes.storage: Keep crêpes and broth separate; 2 days refrigerated.
recipes.freezing: Freeze plain crêpes up to 1 month.
recipes.reheating: Reheat the broth; assemble fresh.
chefTips: 'Mbusse' means soaked — the hot broth softens the cheese-filled crêpes into silky ribbons.
Roll the crêpes tightly so they hold together in the broth.
variations: A Teramo Christmas starter — a richer capon broth is traditional.

recipes.title: Virtù Teramane
recipes.description: Virtù Teramane from Abruzzo. A vegetable & pasta soup preparation built on small pasta or broken spaghetti, borlotti or cannellini beans, onion, potato, seasonal vegetables.

steps.text: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil 10 minutes.
Add the potato, tomatoes and Parmigiano rind and cover with water or light stock. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add the rest of the vegetables and the beans and simmer 20 minutes more until everything is tender; mash a little for body.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente, loosening with water as needed.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat. Serve with a spoon of pesto (Genoese-style) or grated Parmigiano and olive oil.

recipes.freezing: Freeze without pasta up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with extra water or stock.
chefTips: Minestrone is better after resting — make it ahead.
A Parmigiano rind simmered in gives savoury depth for free.
variations: Genoese minestrone finishes with a spoon of pesto.
Rice instead of pasta in parts of Lombardy and Veneto.
commonMistakes: Cooking the pasta separately and losing the starch.

recipes.title: Spaghetti alla Mugnaia
recipes.description: Spaghetti alla Mugnaia from Abruzzo. A garlic & tomato with hand-rolled pici preparation built on '00' or bread flour, warm water, olive oil, salt.

items.name: large garlic cloves
items.note: aglione if you can get it, sliced

steps.text: Make a firm dough with the pici ingredients, knead 10 minutes, and rest 30 minutes covered.
Roll pieces into thick, uneven spaghetti-like strands with your palms — pici are meant to be rustic.
For the sauce, warm the sliced garlic very gently in the oil until soft and sweet, not coloured, then add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer 20 minutes.
Cook the pici in well-salted water 4–6 minutes until springy; reserve water.
Toss the pici through the sauce with a little pasta water. Serve with grated Pecorino Toscano.

recipes.storage: Sauce keeps 4 days; fresh pici keep 1 day or freeze.
recipes.freezing: Freeze fresh pici on a tray, then bag, up to 1 month.
recipes.reheating: Reheat the sauce and cook fresh pici to serve.
chefTips: Aglione is a giant, mellow garlic — regular garlic works, just cook it low and slow so it turns sweet.
Pici want a firm dough and no egg; the chew is the point.
variations: Pici all'aglione, cacio e pepe, or with a duck ragù are the Val di Chiana classics.
Dried pici from a packet cut the work.
commonMistakes: Browning the garlic, which turns it bitter.

recipes.description: Cicatielli con Baccalà from Molise. A quick pantry sauce preparation built on cicatielli, good tuna in olive oil, cherry tomatoes, garlic cloves, capers, black olives.

steps.text: Soften the garlic and chilli in the oil. Add the tomatoes and cook 10–12 minutes until collapsed.
Stir in the tuna in big flakes, the capers and olives; warm through 3 minutes.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the cicatielli. Cook 6–9 minutes until firm to the bite. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through with a little pasta water and the parsley.
No cheese with fish.

recipes.description: Sagne e Fagioli from Abruzzo. A pasta & legume soup preparation built on sagne, cooked borlotti beans, onion, garlic cloves, celery stalk, tinned tomatoes, rosemary.

items.name: cooked borlotti beans
items.note: with their liquid, or 250 g dried, soaked

steps.text: Sweat the onion, garlic and celery in the oil until soft.
Add the tomatoes, rosemary and Parmigiano rind if using, and cook 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Vincisgrassi
recipes.description: Vincisgrassi from Marche. A layered & baked preparation built on fresh lasagne sheets, ragù bolognese, béchamel, parmigiano-reggiano, butter.

items.note: 50 g butter, 50 g flour, 800 ml milk, nutmeg

Press the batter through a spätzle press or colander into a pot of salted boiling water.

Serve with grated cheese.

recipes.title: Penne alla Vodka with Prosciutto
recipes.description: Penne alla Vodka with Prosciutto from Italian-American, Bronx, New York. A creamy tomato sauce preparation built on penne, pancetta or prosciutto, small onion, tomato purée, vodka, double cream, parmigiano-reggiano.

steps.text: Soften the onion (and pancetta) in a little oil until translucent.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook 3–4 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet, not raw.
Add the vodka and simmer 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol.
Stir in the cream and chilli and simmer to a smooth, pale-orange sauce.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the penne. Cook al dente so the quills keep their bite. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through with pasta water and the Parmigiano until glossy.

recipes.freezing: Freezes acceptably up to 1 month; whisk on reheating.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of milk or water.
chefTips: Cooking the tomato purée properly before the liquid goes in removes the tinny edge.

recipes.title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
recipes.description: Spaghetti and Meatballs from Bronx, New York. A meatballs in tomato sauce preparation built on minced beef, minced pork, fresh breadcrumbs, egg, pecorino romano, garlic cloves, parsley.

steps.text: Mix the meatball ingredients gently — don't compact them — and roll into balls a little smaller than a golf ball.
Brown them in the oil in batches; set aside.

Return the meatballs and simmer gently 40 minutes, turning once, until tender and the sauce is thick.

commonMistakes: Over-mixing and over-rolling, making them dense.

recipes.title: Linguine with White Clam Sauce
recipes.description: Linguine with White Clam Sauce from Bronx, New York. A italian-american clam sauce preparation built on linguine, littleneck clams, garlic cloves, dry white wine, extra-virgin olive oil, butter, chilli flakes.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli until fragrant.
Add the wine and clam juice and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the clams, cover, and steam 4–6 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Swirl in the butter and most of the parsley.
Cook the pasta 2 minutes short and finish it in the pan with a little pasta water, tossing so the sauce clings.

commonMistakes: Overcooking the clams.
Not finishing the pasta in the pan.

recipes.title: Fettuccine Alfredo alla Arthur Avenue
recipes.description: Fettuccine Alfredo alla Arthur Avenue from Bronx, New York. A melted cheese sauce preparation built on fettuccine, parmigiano-reggiano (plenty of it), double cream or milk, parmigiano-reggiano, walnuts.

steps.text: Warm the cream gently in a wide pan and melt in the cheese to a smooth sauce.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the fettuccine. Fresh fettuccine need 2–3 minutes. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a little pasta water and the Parmigiano.
Finish with black pepper and the toasted walnuts.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; loosen well on reheating.
recipes.freezing: Not recommended.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with extra milk.
chefTips: Keep the heat low — a boiled cheese sauce turns grainy.

variations: Add a handful of wilted spinach or a spoon of mascarpone for richness.

commonMistakes: Overheating the cheese.

recipes.title: Stuffed Shells with Sunday Sauce
recipes.description: Stuffed Shells with Sunday Sauce from Bronx, New York. A stuffed & baked preparation built on large pasta shells or manicotti tubes, ricotta, egg, parmigiano-reggiano, mozzarella, parsley or basil.

items.name: large pasta shells or manicotti tubes

steps.text: Boil the shells until just pliable, 2 minutes under al dente; drain and cool on a tray.
Mix the ricotta, egg, Parmigiano, mozzarella, herbs and seasoning into a smooth filling.
Spread a layer of sauce in a baking dish. Pipe or spoon the filling into each shell and nestle them in, seam up.
Spoon over more sauce (leave the tops peeking through), scatter with Parmigiano.
Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 30–35 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.freezing: Freeze assembled and unbaked up to 2 months.

Undercook the shells so they survive filling and baking.
variations: Add cooked spinach to the filling.
Manicotti uses the same filling rolled in crêpes or tubes.
commonMistakes: Overfilling so they split.
Skipping the base layer of sauce, so they stick.

recipes.title: Manicotti al Forno

recipes.title: Lasagna alla Nonna Bronx
recipes.description: Lasagna alla Nonna Bronx from Bronx, New York. A layered & baked preparation built on fresh lasagne sheets, ragù bolognese, béchamel, parmigiano-reggiano, butter.

items.name: béchamel
items.note: 50 g butter, 50 g flour, 800 ml milk, nutmeg

steps.text: Make the béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add warm milk gradually to a pourable sauce. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F. Butter a baking dish.
Spread a little béchamel on the base. Layer: pasta, ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano. Repeat for 5–6 thin layers.
Finish with béchamel and a generous layer of Parmigiano.
Bake 40–45 minutes until deep golden and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting — this is not optional if you want clean slices.

recipes.title: Ravioli with Tomato Basil Sauce
recipes.description: Ravioli with Tomato Basil Sauce from Bronx, New York. A filled pasta in brown butter preparation built on fresh cheese ravioli.

Cook the cheese ravioli 3–4 minutes until they float and the edges are tender.

Serve with Parmigiano and pepper.

variations: Brown a few chopped hazelnuts or amaretti in the butter for pumpkin fillings.
A whisper of nutmeg suits ricotta fillings.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard and splitting the pasta.

recipes.title: Cavatelli with Broccoli Rabe and Sausage
recipes.description: Cavatelli with Broccoli Rabe and Sausage from Bronx, New York. A sausage & greens preparation built on cavatelli, coarse pork sausage, broccoli rabe, garlic cloves, chilli flakes, extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Blanch the greens 3 minutes in salted water; lift out (keep the water) and chop.
Brown the crumbled sausage in the oil until caught in places. Add the garlic and chilli.
Add the greens and toss to coat, loosening with a little of the blanching water.
Cook the pasta in the greens' water and finish it in the pan a minute early.
Serve with Pecorino.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water.

variations: Broccoli rabe, turnip tops or kale all work.

commonMistakes: Boiling the sausage grey instead of browning it.

recipes.title: Penne Scarpariello

items.note: boned, cut into chunks (or use just the sauce)

items.name: handful pickled cherry peppers
items.note: sliced, plus a splash of their brine

recipes.title: Eggplant Rollatini with Pasta

items.note: cooked al dente, tossed in a little sauce

steps.text: Salt the aubergine slices 30 minutes, pat dry, then grill or fry until pliable and lightly coloured.
Mix the ricotta, egg, Parmigiano, mozzarella and basil into a filling.
Put a spoon of filling on each slice and roll up.
Spread sauce in a dish, add the dressed pasta as a bed, sit the rolls on top seam-down, spoon over more sauce and scatter with Parmigiano.
Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 30–35 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.freezing: Freeze assembled and unbaked up to 2 months.

commonMistakes: Aubergine slices too firm to roll.

recipes.title: Sausage and Peppers Rigatoni
recipes.description: Sausage and Peppers Rigatoni from Bronx, New York. A quick sausage ragù preparation built on fresh rigatoni, coarse pork sausage, onion, dry white wine, passata, rosemary, extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil. Add the crumbled sausage and brown well.
Add the wine and reduce, then the passata and rosemary. Simmer 25–30 minutes to a thick sauce.
Cook the pasta, reserving a mugful of water.
Toss the pasta through the ragù with a little pasta water.

recipes.title: Bucatini with Sunday Meat Sauce

Add the crushed tomatoes, a rinse of water from the tins, and the basil. Return the ribs and sausages.
Simmer on the lowest heat 3–4 hours, stirring occasionally, adding the meatballs for the last hour.

Add the tomatoes, rosemary and Parmigiano rind if using, and cook 5 minutes.
Add the cannellini beans with enough water or stock to cover generously and simmer 20 minutes.
Purée about a third of the soup and stir it back in for body.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente, adding water if it gets too thick.

recipes.title: Lobster Fra Diavolo

Stir in the tuna in big flakes, the capers and olives; warm through 3 minutes.

No cheese with fish.

Fresh tomato in summer, tinned in winter.

commonMistakes: Rushing the simmer — the sauce stays watery and raw-tasting.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Aglio, Olio e Peperoncino
recipes.description: Spaghetti Aglio, Olio e Peperoncino from Naples, Campania. A boiled & emulsified preparation built on spaghetti, garlic cloves, extra-virgin olive oil, dried chilli flakes, large handful flat-leaf parsley.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the spaghetti. Cook until al dente, about 1 minute less than the packet. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile warm the oil with the garlic over medium-low heat until the garlic is pale gold — never brown.
Add the chilli and cook 30 seconds, then add 3 tablespoons of pasta water and swirl to emulsify.
Toss the drained pasta in the pan with the parsley, adding pasta water until glossy.
Serve at once — no cheese.

recipes.storage: Eat fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.freezing: Not suitable.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water.
chefTips: Take the garlic off before it colours past pale gold; bitter garlic ruins the dish.
The emulsion of oil and pasta water is what stops it being greasy.
variations: Add a few chopped anchovies with the garlic for depth.
Toasted breadcrumbs on top for crunch.
commonMistakes: Browning the garlic.
Not emulsifying with pasta water — the oil slides off.

recipes.title: Pasta al Burro e Parmigiano
recipes.description: Pasta al Burro e Parmigiano from Northern Italy. A melted cheese sauce preparation built on tagliatelle, parmigiano-reggiano, double cream or milk, parmigiano-reggiano, walnuts.

steps.text: Warm the cream gently in a wide pan and melt in the cheese to a smooth sauce.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the tagliatelle. Fresh tagliatelle need 2–3 minutes; they cling to ragù. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a little pasta water and the Parmigiano.
Finish with black pepper and the toasted walnuts.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; loosen well on reheating.
recipes.freezing: Not recommended.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with extra milk.
chefTips: Keep the heat low — a boiled cheese sauce turns grainy.
A little pasta water keeps it from being cloying.
variations: Add a handful of wilted spinach or a spoon of mascarpone for richness.
Swap the walnuts for a drizzle of honey with blue cheese.
commonMistakes: Overheating the cheese.
No pasta water, so it sets stiff on the plate.

recipes.title: Ravioli Ricotta e Spinaci
recipes.description: Ravioli Ricotta e Spinaci from Central Italy. A filled pasta in brown butter preparation built on fresh ricotta and spinach ravioli.

steps.text: Bring a wide pan of well-salted water to a gentle boil — a hard boil tears filled pasta.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan with the sage and cook until the butter smells nutty and the sage crisps.
Cook the ricotta and spinach ravioli 3–4 minutes until they float and the edges are tender.
Lift them straight into the butter with a little pasta water and swirl to emulsify into a glossy sauce.
Serve with Parmigiano and pepper.

recipes.freezing: Freeze the uncooked filled pasta up to 1 month; cook from frozen.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently in a little butter and water.
chefTips: Keep the water at a gentle simmer so the parcels don't burst.
A spoon of pasta water in the butter turns it from greasy to silky.
variations: Brown a few chopped hazelnuts or amaretti in the butter for pumpkin fillings.
A whisper of nutmeg suits ricotta fillings.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard and splitting the pasta.
Letting the butter burn past nut-brown to black.

recipes.title: Gnocchi di Patate al Sugo
recipes.description: Gnocchi di Patate al Sugo from Italy. A simmered tomato preparation built on potato gnocchi, ripe tomatoes, garlic cloves, large bunch basil, extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the garlic until fragrant, then discard the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them, with a few basil leaves and a pinch of salt. Simmer 20–25 minutes until thick and sweet.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the potato gnocchi. Cook until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a little pasta water and the rest of the basil, torn.
Finish with olive oil and grated Parmigiano.

recipes.freezing: Freeze the sauce up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently and toss with fresh pasta.
chefTips: A pinch of sugar rounds out sharp out-of-season tomatoes.
Tear the basil in at the end so it stays fragrant.
variations: Stir in a knob of butter at the end for a silkier sauce (Marcella-style).
commonMistakes: Rushing the simmer — the sauce stays watery and raw-tasting.

recipes.description: Spaghetti con Colatura di Alici from Cetara, Campania. A raw colatura di alici preparation built on spaghetti or linguine, colatura di alici (cetara anchovy syrup), garlic cloves, extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Warm the oil gently with the garlic and chilli; discard the garlic. Take off the heat.
Cook the pasta in UNSALTED water — the colatura is very salty. Reserve a mugful.
In the serving bowl, whisk the colatura with the warm garlic oil and a spoon of pasta water into an emulsion.
Toss the drained pasta through with the parsley, loosening with pasta water.
Serve at once. No cheese.

recipes.freezing: Not suitable.
recipes.reheating: Not recommended.
chefTips: Don't salt the pasta water — colatura is a concentrated anchovy syrup and does the seasoning.
Keep everything off the heat once the colatura is in; cooking it turns it harsh.
variations: A few toasted breadcrumbs for crunch.
Cetara serves it especially on Christmas Eve.
commonMistakes: Salting the water.
Cooking the sauce.

recipes.title: Pasta con Fave e Pecorino
recipes.description: Pasta con Fave e Pecorino from Lazio. A fresh broad beans & pecorino preparation built on spaghetti, broad beans in pod, spring onion or small onion, guanciale or pancetta, young pecorino.

steps.text: Blanch the podded broad beans 1 minute and slip off the grey skins (double-podding) for sweetness and colour.
Soften the onion (and guanciale) in the oil. Add the beans and a splash of water and cook 4–5 minutes, crushing a few.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil and cook the spaghetti. Cook until al dente, about 1 minute less than the packet. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through with pasta water and the grated pecorino until it clings.
Finish with mint, pecorino shavings and pepper.

recipes.freezing: Freeze the podded beans, not the finished dish.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.
chefTips: Double-pod the beans unless they are tiny and new — the skins are bitter.
A Roman spring dish; keep it light and green.
variations: Peas or a mix of peas and beans.
Leave out the guanciale for a vegetarian plate.
commonMistakes: Skipping the double-podding.
Overcooking the beans to khaki.

recipes.title: Minestra Maritata con Pasta
recipes.description: Minestra Maritata con Pasta from Campania. A broth with greens & tiny meatballs preparation built on good chicken broth, escarole or curly endive, small pasta, minced beef and pork, egg, parmigiano-reggiano.

items.name: escarole or curly endive
items.note: plus a little cabbage or chard

steps.text: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, Parmigiano and seasoning; roll into tiny meatballs the size of a marble.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and poach the meatballs 8–10 minutes until cooked.
Add the chopped greens and simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente.
Serve very hot with plenty of grated Parmigiano.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; add fresh pasta or expect it to thicken.
recipes.freezing: Freeze broth and meatballs (no pasta) up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently, adding broth.
chefTips: 'Wedding' is a mistranslation of 'minestra maritata' — the marriage is of greens and meat, not a ceremony.
Keep the meatballs tiny so several land in every spoonful.
variations: Southern Italian 'minestra maritata' uses mixed pork cuts and lots of bitter greens, no pasta.
A beaten egg stirred in at the end (stracciatella-style).
commonMistakes: Meatballs too large.
Cooking the pasta so far ahead it swells and drinks the broth.

recipes.title: Lasagne di Pane Carasau
recipes.description: Lasagne di Pane Carasau from Sardinia. A bread & cheese bake preparation built on stale country bread or carasau, fresh pecorino or caciotta, aged pecorino, rich lamb or beef broth, saffron.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Layer the bread and sliced cheese in a deep dish, finishing with grated pecorino.
Ladle the hot broth (with saffron if using) evenly over until the bread is soaked but not swimming.
Bake 35–40 minutes until set, golden and bubbling at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes; serve in wedges.

recipes.freezing: Freeze cooked portions up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered at 170°C / 340°F for 20 minutes.
chefTips: Zuppa gallurese is 'zuppa' in the old sense — soaked bread, not a liquid soup.
The broth must be well-flavoured; it is doing most of the seasoning.
variations: Add chopped parsley and mint between the layers.
Sardinian carasau bread gives a lighter, crisper result.
commonMistakes: Too much broth, turning it to mush.
Weak broth, leaving it bland.

recipes.title: Ravioli di Zucca alla Ferrarese
recipes.description: Ravioli di Zucca alla Ferrarese from Ferrara, Emilia-Romagna. A pumpkin-filled pasta in butter preparation built on pumpkin or butternut, amaretti biscuits, parmigiano-reggiano, mostarda di frutta.

steps.text: Dry out the roasted pumpkin in a pan if wet, then mix with the amaretti, Parmigiano, mostarda if using, nutmeg and salt. It should be thick enough to pipe.
Make and rest the egg pasta 30 minutes, then roll it very thin.
Pipe filling in small mounds, fold and seal well, and cut into tortelli or cappellacci. Keep them dusted and covered.
Cook in gently simmering salted water 3–4 minutes until the edges are tender.
Brown the butter with the sage. Lift the pasta into the butter with a spoon of pasta water and swirl.
Serve with Parmigiano; a Mantua plate leans slightly sweet from the amaretti and mostarda.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate cooked up to 1 day.
recipes.freezing: Freeze uncooked on a tray up to 1 month; cook from frozen.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently in butter and water.
chefTips: Dry the pumpkin well — a wet filling makes sealing impossible and bursts on cooking.
Gentle simmer, firm seals.
variations: Ferrara's cappellacci skip the mostarda and lean savoury.
A little crushed amaretti over the top at the end.
commonMistakes: Wet filling.
Boiling hard.

recipes.title: Pasta con Sugo di Coniglio
recipes.description: Pasta con Sugo di Coniglio from Ischia, Campania. A braised meat ragù preparation built on rabbit (jointed), onion, garlic cloves, carrot, red wine, crushed tomatoes, rosemary, extra-virgin olive oil.

items.name: sprig rosemary, olives and white wine

steps.text: Brown the rabbit (jointed) in the oil in batches until well coloured; set aside.
Soften the onion, garlic and carrot in the same pot for 8 minutes.
Return the meat, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes and rosemary, olives and white wine, season, and braise on low heat 1.5–2 hours until the meat is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted water; reserve a mugful of water.
Toss the pasta through the ragù with a little pasta water. Serve with grated Pecorino.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of stock or water.
chefTips: Brown the rabbit (jointed) properly — colour is flavour in a braised ragù.
Keep the heat low and give it time; the meat should shred, not chew.
variations: A strip of orange or lemon peel in the braise lifts gamey meats.
Swap the fresh ribbons for a sturdy tube if that is the local shape.
commonMistakes: Crowding the pan when browning, so the meat steams grey.
Rushing the braise.

recipes.title: Gnocchi di Ricotta alla Romana
recipes.description: Gnocchi di Ricotta alla Romana from Lazio. A ricotta dumplings in butter preparation built on ricotta, parmigiano-reggiano, egg yolk, '00' flour, butter, sage leaves.

items.name: '00' flour
items.note: plus more for rolling, or fine semolina to coat

steps.text: Mix the ricotta, Parmigiano, yolk, a little flour, nutmeg and salt into a soft dough that just holds.
Roll into small dumplings and dust well (or bed them in semolina and chill several hours, gnudi-style).
Poach gently in salted water 2–3 minutes until they float — cook one first to check it holds.
Brown the butter with the sage.
Lift the dumplings into the sage butter with a spoon of cooking water and swirl to coat. Serve with Parmigiano.

recipes.freezing: Freeze uncooked on a tray, then bag, up to 1 month.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently in butter.
chefTips: Drain the ricotta hard — wet ricotta means you need more flour, and more flour means rubber.
A gentle poach only; a rolling boil tears them.
variations: Add chopped cooked spinach for gnudi verdi.
Semolina gnocchi alla romana: set a cooked semolina paste, cut into discs, dot with butter and Parmesan and bake until golden.
commonMistakes: Too much flour.
Boiling hard.

recipes.title: Zuppa di Ceci e Tagliatelle
recipes.description: Zuppa di Ceci e Tagliatelle from Umbria. A pasta & legume soup preparation built on tagliatelle, cooked chickpeas, onion, garlic cloves, celery stalk, tinned tomatoes, rosemary.

items.name: cooked chickpeas
items.note: with their liquid, or 250 g dried, soaked

steps.text: Sweat the onion, garlic and celery in the oil until soft.
Add the tomatoes, rosemary and Parmigiano rind if using, and cook 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas with enough water or stock to cover generously and simmer 20 minutes.
Purée about a third of the soup and stir it back in for body.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente, adding water if it gets too thick.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then serve with a thread of olive oil and pepper.

recipes.storage: Thickens overnight; loosen with water. Keeps 3 days.
recipes.freezing: Freeze without pasta up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with extra water or stock, stirring.
chefTips: Blending part of the beans is the trick to a creamy soup without cream.
It should be spoonable but not soupy — 'minestra', not brodo.
variations: Add pancetta or a ham bone for a meatier pot.
Short pasta scraps ('pasta mista') are traditional and stop it feeling like a pasta bowl.
commonMistakes: Cooking the pasta separately and losing the starch that thickens the soup.
Letting it dry out into a stew after resting.

recipes.title: Pasta al Forno della Domenica
recipes.description: Pasta al Forno della Domenica from Southern Italy. A baked (al forno) preparation built on rigatoni, tomato or meat ragù, fresh mozzarella or fior di latte, parmigiano-reggiano, hard-boiled eggs.

items.name: fresh mozzarella or fior di latte

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Cook the pasta 3 minutes short of al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta with two-thirds of the ragù.
Layer half in an oiled baking dish with mozzarella, Parmigiano and the optional egg and salami; repeat.
Finish with the remaining ragù and a heavy layer of Parmigiano.
Bake 30–35 minutes until bubbling with a browned, crisp top.
Rest 10–15 minutes before cutting so it holds its shape.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and reheats very well.
recipes.freezing: Freeze cooked portions up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered at 180°C / 350°F for 20 minutes.
chefTips: Undercook the pasta — it keeps cooking in the oven.
Drain the mozzarella well or the bake turns watery.
variations: Anelletti al forno (Palermo) presses the same idea into a tin and turns it out.
A layer of fried aubergine makes it a 'pasta 'ncasciata'.
commonMistakes: Fully cooking the pasta first, so it goes mushy.
Cutting straight from the oven so it collapses.

recipes.title: Conchiglie Ripiene di Ricotta
recipes.description: Conchiglie Ripiene di Ricotta from Southern Italy. A stuffed & baked preparation built on large pasta shells or manicotti tubes, ricotta, egg, parmigiano-reggiano, mozzarella, parsley or basil.

items.name: large pasta shells or manicotti tubes

steps.text: Boil the shells until just pliable, 2 minutes under al dente; drain and cool on a tray.
Mix the ricotta, egg, Parmigiano, mozzarella, herbs and seasoning into a smooth filling.
Spread a layer of sauce in a baking dish. Pipe or spoon the filling into each shell and nestle them in, seam up.
Spoon over more sauce (leave the tops peeking through), scatter with Parmigiano.
Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 30–35 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.freezing: Freeze assembled and unbaked up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat covered at 180°C / 350°F for 20–25 minutes.
chefTips: Drain the ricotta hard — wet ricotta makes a sloppy bake.
Undercook the shells so they survive filling and baking.
variations: Add cooked spinach to the filling.
Manicotti uses the same filling rolled in crêpes or tubes.
commonMistakes: Overfilling so they split.
Skipping the base layer of sauce, so they stick.

recipes.title: Lasagnette al Pesto
recipes.description: Lasagnette al Pesto from Liguria. A raw pounded sauce preparation built on basil leaves, garlic cloves, pine nuts, parmigiano-reggiano, pecorino sardo, mild extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Pound the garlic and a pinch of coarse salt to a paste in a mortar. Add the pine nuts and crush.
Add the basil a little at a time, grinding against the sides with a circular motion until you have a bright green cream.
Work in the cheeses, then trickle in the oil, stirring, until loose and glossy. Do not heat it.
Boil the potatoes 5 minutes, add the green beans for 3 minutes, then add the pasta and cook until al dente.
Loosen the pesto with a spoonful of pasta water in the serving bowl. Drain the pasta and vegetables, toss through, and serve warm — never hot enough to cook the pesto.

recipes.storage: Cover the surface with oil; keeps 3 days refrigerated.
recipes.freezing: Freeze without cheese up to 3 months; stir cheese in after thawing.
recipes.reheating: Do not reheat — dress fresh pasta or serve at room temperature.
chefTips: Keep everything cool. Heat and over-processing turn pesto dark and bitter.
The potatoes and beans are not optional in Liguria — they make the dish.
variations: A blender works if you pulse in short bursts and keep the bowl cold.
Trofie, trenette and mandilli are the classic shapes.
commonMistakes: Blitzing to a hot purée in a food processor.
Tossing into screaming-hot pasta, which greys the sauce.

recipes.title: Tagliolini in Brodo di Cappone
recipes.description: Tagliolini in Brodo di Cappone from Northern Italy. A filled pasta in clear broth preparation built on fresh tagliolini, clear capon or chicken broth, parmigiano-reggiano.

steps.text: Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and check the seasoning.
Slip in the tagliolini and cook until they float and the pasta is tender, about 3–4 minutes for fresh.
Ladle into warm bowls with plenty of broth.
Serve with grated Parmigiano at the table.

recipes.storage: Keep pasta and broth separate; combine when serving. 2 days refrigerated.
recipes.freezing: Freeze broth and uncooked pasta separately up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat the broth, then cook the pasta in it fresh.
chefTips: The broth must be genuinely good and clear — it is half the dish.
Cook the pasta right in the broth so it seasons the bowl.
variations: 'In brodo' for feast days; the same pasta is served 'asciutti' with butter on other days.
Passatelli (a Parmesan-and-crumb dough pressed through a ricer) is made the same way.
commonMistakes: Boiling the broth hard and clouding it.
Over-filling the bowl with pasta and skimping on broth.

recipes.title: Risotto alla Pescatora
recipes.description: Risotto alla Pescatora from Adriatic Italy. A risotto (mantecato) preparation built on carnaroli or arborio rice, small onion, hot light stock, dry white wine, extra-virgin olive oil or butter.

steps.text: Sweat the onion in the fat until soft and translucent, without colour.
Add the rice and toast 2 minutes until the grains are hot and slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, waiting until each addition is nearly absorbed before the next. This takes 16–18 minutes; the rice should stay al dente.
Fold through the cooked seafood (steam the shellfish open separately and add their strained liquor to the stock). No cheese.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve 'all'onda' — loose enough to ripple on the plate.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 1 month; best repurposed as arancini.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with extra stock, stirring, or fry as cakes.
chefTips: Keep the stock hot — cold stock stalls the cook and makes it gluey.
The 'mantecatura' (beating in cold fat off the heat) is what makes it creamy, not cream.
variations: Leftover risotto sets and fries into 'risotto al salto' or arancini.
A spoon of bone marrow is the old Milanese touch.
commonMistakes: Adding all the stock at once.
Cooking the rice to mush — stop while it has bite.

recipes.title: Orzotto ai Funghi
recipes.description: Orzotto ai Funghi from Northern Italy. A barley risotto-style preparation built on pearl barley, mushrooms, onion, white wine, hot vegetable or chicken stock, butter, parmigiano-reggiano.

steps.text: Sear the mushrooms in the oil until browned; set aside.
Soften the onion, add the barley and toast 2 minutes.
Add the wine and let it absorb, then add hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often, for about 35–40 minutes until the barley is tender but chewy.
Stir the mushrooms back in for the last 5 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the butter and Parmigiano. Rest 2 minutes and serve loose.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 2 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with extra stock, stirring.
chefTips: Barley never goes as creamy as rice — a little extra stirring and the butter finish get it there.
It reheats far better than a rice risotto.
variations: Trentino orzotto often adds Speck and cabbage or squash.
Keep it vegetarian with just mushrooms and thyme.
commonMistakes: Under-cooking the barley — it should be tender, not bullet-hard.
Skipping the butter-and-cheese finish.

recipes.title: Zuppa di Farro con Pasta

steps.text: Sweat the onion, garlic and celery in the oil until soft.

recipes.title: Minestrone alla Genovese
recipes.description: Minestrone alla Genovese from Liguria. A vegetable & pasta soup preparation built on small pasta or broken spaghetti, borlotti or cannellini beans, onion, potato, seasonal vegetables.

steps.text: Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in the oil 10 minutes.
Add the potato, tomatoes and Parmigiano rind and cover with water or light stock. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add the rest of the vegetables and the beans and simmer 20 minutes more until everything is tender; mash a little for body.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente, loosening with water as needed.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat. Serve with a spoon of pesto (Genoese-style) or grated Parmigiano and olive oil.

recipes.freezing: Freeze without pasta up to 3 months.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with extra water or stock.
chefTips: Minestrone is better after resting — make it ahead.
A Parmigiano rind simmered in gives savoury depth for free.
variations: Genoese minestrone finishes with a spoon of pesto.
Rice instead of pasta in parts of Lombardy and Veneto.

recipes.title: Pasta e Cavolfiore
recipes.description: Pasta e Cavolfiore from Southern Italy. A braised cauliflower preparation built on maccheroni, cauliflower, onion, sultanas, pine nuts, anchovy fillets, saffron, extra-virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Boil the cauliflower in salted water until just tender; scoop out (keep the water) and set aside.
Soften the onion in the oil, melt in the anchovies, then add the sultanas, pine nuts and saffron water.
Add the cauliflower and crush it lightly so some breaks down into a sauce. Loosen with cauliflower water.
Cook the pasta in the cauliflower water; drain and toss through the pan.
Serve with toasted breadcrumbs.

recipes.freezing: Freeze up to 1 month.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.
chefTips: 'Arriminata' means stirred/mashed — you want half sauce, half florets.
The saffron and sultanas make it unmistakably Palermitano.
variations: Add a little tomato purée for a rosy version.
commonMistakes: Leaving the cauliflower in big firm lumps with no sauce.
